ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, with point A of square ABCD as the center and AB as the radius, draw the arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$. Choose a point F on arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$ such that $DF=DC$, and let point E be another point on arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$ (not coinciding with points D or F). What is the value of $\angle DEF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw AE and AF.\\
$\because$ With A as the center of the circle and AB as the radius, construct arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$, and choose a point F on arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$ such that DF=DC.\\
$\therefore$AD=AE=AF=DF,\\
$\therefore$$\triangle$ADF is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$DAF=$60^\circ$, $\angle$ADE=$\angle$DEA, $\angle$AEF=$\angle$AFE,\\
$\because$$\angle$DAE+$\angle$ADE+$\angle$DEA=$180^\circ$, then 2$\angle$ADE=$180^\circ$−$\angle$DAE,\\
$\angle$EAF+$\angle$AEF+$\angle$AFE=$180^\circ$, then 2$\angle$AEF=$180^\circ$−$\angle$EAF,\\
$\therefore$2$\angle$ADE+2$\angle$AEF=$360^\circ$−($\angle$DAE+$\angle$EAF)=$360^\circ$−$\angle$DAF=$300^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$ADE+$\angle$AEF=$150^\circ$, thus $\angle$DEF=\boxed{150^\circ}.

令 E=(cos θ, sin θ)。由图像可见 E 在 D 与 F 之间的圆弧上，所以 π/6<θ<π/2。用复平面表示单位圆点，D=e^{iπ/2}，F=e^{iπ/6}，E=e^{iθ}。向量 ED 的方向由 e^{iπ/2}-e^{iθ} 给出，其方向角为 θ/2+3π/4。向量 EF 的方向由 e^{iπ/6}-e^{iθ} 给出，其方向角可取 θ/2-5π/12。两方向角之差为 (θ/2+3π/4)-(θ/2-5π/12)=7π/6，因此两条射线之间的较小夹角为 2π-7π/6=5π/6=150°。所以 ∠DEF=150°。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, with point A of square ABCD as the center and AB as the radius, draw the arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$. Choose a point F on arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$ such that $DF=DC$, and let point E be another point on arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$ (not coinciding with points D or F). What is the value of $\angle DEF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw AE and AF.\\
$\because$ With A as the center of the circle and AB as the radius, construct arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$, and choose a point F on arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$ such that $DF=DC.\\
$\therefore$ AD=AE=AF=DF,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ADF$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DAF=60^\circ$, $\angle ADE=\angle DEA$, $\angle AEF=\angle AFE$,\\
$\because$ $\angle DAE+\angle ADE+\angle DEA=180^\circ$, then $2\angle ADE=180^\circ-\angle DAE$,\\
$\angle EAF+\angle AEF+\angle AFE=180^\circ$, then $2\angle AEF=180^\circ-\angle EAF$,\\
$\therefore$ $2\angle ADE+2\angle AEF=360^\circ-(\angle DAE+\angle EAF)=360^\circ-\angle DAF=300^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADE+\angle AEF=150^\circ$, thus $\angle DEF=\boxed{150^\circ}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is square ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left. The quarter-circle arc centered at A goes from D through E and F to B; in the figure, E is located on the smaller arc DF between D and F, and line segments DE and EF are drawn.

Reasoning: ABCD is a square, so DC = AD = AB. F is on the arc centered at A with radius AB, therefore AF = AB = AD. Also, from the condition DF = DC, and DC = AD, so DF = AD. Thus AD = AF = DF, triangle ADF is an equilateral triangle, so the central angle ∠DAF = 60°, that is, the measure of the smaller arc DF is 60°. Since in the figure E is on the smaller arc DF, ∠DEF is an inscribed angle, and what it subtends is the other major arc DF, whose measure is 360° - 60° = 300°. An inscribed angle equals half the measure of the arc it subtends, therefore ∠DEF = 300° / 2 = 150°.
